description: Fully managed relational databases for MySQL, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server.
detail: Cloud SQL provides managed relational database instances with automated backups, maintenance, replication options, IAM integration, private networking, and high availability configurations. It is a strong default for traditional application databases that need familiar SQL engines.
benefits: Managed MySQL, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server operations
Automated backups, patching, and high availability options
Works with private IP, IAM, and Google Cloud observability
cons: Instance sizing and connection limits still require planning
Not designed for unlimited horizontal relational scale
useCases: Operational systems that need standard SQL engines
example: A startup migrates a PostgreSQL application from a self-managed VM to Cloud SQL to gain automated backups, private networking, and managed maintenance.

description: PostgreSQL-compatible database for demanding enterprise workloads.
detail: AlloyDB is a fully managed PostgreSQL-compatible database designed for high performance, high availability, analytics acceleration, and AI-ready application development. AlloyDB AI adds vector search and integrations for generative AI applications.
benefits: PostgreSQL compatibility with managed operations
High performance for transactional and analytical workloads
Supports vector search and AI application patterns
cons: Best fit is PostgreSQL workloads, not every relational engine
Migration planning is needed for extensions and operational behavior
useCases: AI-enabled apps using embeddings and vector search
example: A retail platform moves a high-traffic PostgreSQL catalog service to AlloyDB and adds vector similarity search for product recommendations.

description: Globally scalable relational database with strong consistency.
detail: Spanner combines relational SQL, horizontal scale, strong consistency, high availability, and multi-region replication. It is designed for mission-critical applications that need relational semantics without traditional single-instance scaling limits.
benefits: Horizontal relational scale
Strong consistency and high availability
Supports relational, key-value, graph, full-text, and vector patterns
cons: Requires careful schema and key design
Can be more complex and costly than smaller relational options
example: A payments company uses Spanner for a globally replicated ledger that requires strong consistency and uptime across regions.

description: Serverless document database for app development.
detail: Firestore stores JSON-like documents in collections with real-time synchronization, offline support for client apps, automatic scaling, security rules, and serverless operations. It is built for rich web, mobile, and IoT applications.
benefits: Serverless document model
Real-time sync and offline client support
Scales automatically for app workloads
cons: Query patterns must fit document and index design
Complex joins and relational transactions are not its strength
useCases: User profiles, preferences, and activity feeds
example: A field-service app uses Firestore to sync work orders between technicians' phones and the back office, even when devices temporarily go offline.

description: Wide-column database for large low-latency workloads.
detail: Bigtable is a fully managed wide-column database built for massive scale, high throughput, and low-latency reads and writes. It is commonly used for time-series, personalization, fraud detection, IoT, and analytical serving workloads.
benefits: Very high throughput and low latency
Scales to large operational and analytical datasets
Integrates with data and AI services
cons: Requires row-key design expertise
Not intended for ad hoc relational querying
example: An IoT company stores device telemetry in Bigtable so dashboards and anomaly detection services can read recent events with low latency.

description: Managed in-memory data stores for Redis, Valkey, and Memcached patterns.
detail: Memorystore provides managed in-memory caching and data structures for low-latency application access. It supports common caching, session, queue, leaderboard, and vector embedding use cases depending on the selected engine and tier.
benefits: Low-latency in-memory access
Managed operations for common cache engines
Useful for reducing database load
cons: Memory capacity and eviction behavior must be planned
Not a replacement for durable system-of-record databases
example: A gaming service stores live leaderboard data in Memorystore so user score updates are reflected with very low latency.

description: Serverless data warehouse for analytics and AI workloads.
detail: BigQuery is a serverless analytical database and data warehouse for SQL analytics, streaming ingestion, machine learning, governance, and data sharing. It is optimized for large-scale analysis rather than transactional application serving.
benefits: Serverless analytics at large scale
Supports SQL, streaming, ML, and governed data sharing
Separates analytical storage and compute concerns
cons: Not designed for low-latency OLTP transactions
Cost controls require partitioning, clustering, and query discipline
example: A marketing team analyzes clickstream and purchase data in BigQuery to measure campaign performance across millions of events.

description: Managed service for migrating databases to Google Cloud.
detail: Database Migration Service helps migrate MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, and Oracle workloads to Cloud SQL and AlloyDB. It supports guided migration flows and conversion assistance for modernization projects.
benefits: Simplifies database migration planning and execution
Supports common source engines
Targets managed Google Cloud database services
cons: Complex schemas and stored procedures still need assessment
Cutover planning and application testing remain customer responsibilities
useCases: Moving self-managed databases to Cloud SQL
Reducing migration downtime and manual steps
example: An enterprise uses Database Migration Service to migrate a legacy MySQL database to Cloud SQL while validating replication before final cutover.

description: Serverless change data capture and replication service.
detail: Datastream captures and streams database changes from sources such as MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, and Oracle. It is commonly used to replicate operational data into BigQuery or downstream processing systems for near real-time analytics.
benefits: Serverless change data capture
Supports near real-time analytics pipelines
Reduces custom replication code
cons: Requires source database configuration and permissions
Schema evolution and downstream consistency need governance
example: A logistics company streams order database changes into BigQuery with Datastream so operations dashboards update within minutes.

description: Fleet management and health dashboard for Google Cloud databases.
detail: Database Center provides a unified view of managed database fleet health, availability, performance, protection, security, and compliance signals across services such as Cloud SQL, AlloyDB, Spanner, Bigtable, Memorystore, and Firestore.
benefits: Centralized database fleet visibility
Health, cost, security, and performance insights
AI-assisted troubleshooting for supported database services
cons: Works best when database resources follow consistent tagging and governance
Does not replace service-specific operational expertise
useCases: Prioritizing remediation across many database instances
example: A database platform team uses Database Center each morning to identify high-risk instances, backup gaps, and performance anomalies across projects.
